name: Mattenai
overview: Mattenai is a male figure noted in Scripture as a descendant of Bani who had married a foreign wife. Beyond this unique attribute, there is no record of his tribal affiliation or additional personal details. His mention is brief and specific within the biblical text.
namesAndTitles: The name Mattenai is a proper name meaning "gift." This name is not indicated as being given directly by God, but it carries the connotation of a valuable or gracious endowment, as reflected in its Hebrew meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Mattenai as a descendant of Bani, establishing a familial link to this ancestor. No other family relationships are recorded beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Mattenai's significance lies in his identification as part of the post-exilic community dealing with issues of intermarriage, specifically as one who descended from Bani yet had taken a foreign wife. This detail highlights the challenges faced by the returned exiles in maintaining covenantal purity, a theme addressed in the book of Ezra. His mention underscores the communal efforts to uphold God's commands during the restoration period.
